subject: mathematics
question_text: Construct a 3×2 matrix whose elements are defined by aᵢⱼ = ½|i − 3j|.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Set up the general form
steps.margin_note: First mark. A 3×2 matrix has i running 1 to 3 (rows) and j running 1 to 2 (columns) — six entries in all.
lines: with aᵢⱼ = ½|i − 3j|, i = 1,2,3 and j = 1,2

recall.must_convey: That the general 3×2 form is written with i from 1 to 3 and j from 1 to 2.
accept: write the general three by two matrix with i one to three and j one to two
three rows and two columns so six entries
set up the general form first
moodu rows rendu columns, six entries
i goes one to three and j one to two

steps.why: The first subscript is the ROW and the second the column. A 3×2 has more rows than columns, so i has the larger range.

steps.label: Compute the six entries
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Substitute each pair. The modulus makes every entry non-negative, so a negative answer means a slip.

recall.must_convey: That the six entries are computed as 1, 5/2, 1/2, 2, 0, 3/2 and placed in the right positions.
accept: substitute each i and j pair to get one five halves one half two zero and three halves
the modulus keeps every entry non negative
compute all six entries and place them
the six values fill the matrix

steps.why: a₃₁ = ½|3 − 3| = 0 is the one entry that vanishes — worth noting, because a zero can look like an omission.
common_mistakes: Dropping the modulus and getting negative entries.
